rules.name: Divisibility transitivity
rules.input_form: a divides b and b divides c
preconditions: All divisibility relations are interpreted over integers
rules.operation: Compose divisibility through an intermediate multiple.
examples: 2 divides 6 and 6 divides 24, so 2 divides 24
counterexamples: Replacing one divisibility premise by a nondivisibility statement invalidates the conclusion

rules.name: Euclidean division form
rules.output_form: a = bq + r with 0 <= r < b
rules.operation: Express integer division by quotient and constrained remainder.
counterexamples: 17 = 5*2 + 7 is invalid Euclidean division because the remainder is not less than 5

rules.name: gcd invariance under remainder reduction
rules.operation: Reduce gcd computation by one Euclidean remainder step.
counterexamples: Replacing a mod b with an unrelated remainder breaks the rule

rules.name: Euclidean algorithm termination rule
preconditions: Remainder reduction is applied correctly at each step
rules.operation: Continue remainder reduction until the remainder is zero; return the last nonzero remainder as the gcd.
counterexamples: Stopping before the zero remainder step can miss the gcd

rules.name: Bezout identity
rules.operation: Represent the gcd as an integer linear combination of the two inputs.
counterexamples: Claiming ax + by = 1 for non-coprime a and b is invalid

rules.name: Coprime criterion via gcd
rules.operation: Classify two integers as coprime exactly when their gcd is 1.
examples: 8 and 15 are coprime
counterexamples: 8 and 12 are not coprime because gcd(8,12) = 4

rules.name: Modular inverse existence criterion
rules.operation: Use coprimality to determine whether a multiplicative inverse exists modulo n.
examples: 3 has an inverse modulo 7 because gcd(3,7)=1
counterexamples: 6 has no inverse modulo 9 because gcd(6,9)=3

rules.name: Fundamental theorem of arithmetic
rules.output_form: prime factorization unique up to order
rules.operation: Factor a positive integer into primes uniquely up to permutation of factors.
counterexamples: Writing two different prime factorizations for the same positive integer is invalid up to ordering

rules.name: Chinese remainder compatibility rule
rules.input_form: x congruent a mod m and x congruent b mod n
preconditions: gcd(m,n)=1
rules.operation: Solve a pair of congruences uniquely modulo the product of coprime moduli.
examples: x congruent 1 mod 2 and x congruent 2 mod 3 has a unique solution modulo 6
counterexamples: Using the uniqueness claim when moduli are not coprime is invalid without extra compatibility checks

rules.name: Fermat little theorem pattern
preconditions: p is prime
p does not divide a
rules.operation: Reduce powers modulo a prime using Fermat's little theorem.
examples: 2^4 congruent 1 mod 5
counterexamples: Applying the rule with composite modulus as if it were prime is invalid

rules.name: Linear Diophantine solvability criterion
rules.output_form: integer solution exists iff gcd(a,b) divides c
rules.operation: Use gcd divisibility to decide solvability of a linear Diophantine equation.
examples: 6x + 9y = 3 has integer solutions because gcd(6,9)=3 divides 3
counterexamples: 6x + 9y = 4 has no integer solution because 3 does not divide 4

rules.name: Euler phi function on prime powers
preconditions: p is prime
rules.operation: Count integers up to p^k that are coprime to p^k.
counterexamples: Treating phi(p^k) as p^k for k >= 1 is invalid

rules.name: Divisor-count function from prime exponents
preconditions: Prime factorization of n is known
rules.operation: Compute the divisor-count function from prime exponents.
counterexamples: Summing exponents instead of multiplying shifted exponents is invalid

rules.name: Quadratic residue criterion by square congruence
preconditions: p is an odd prime in the standard residue setting
rules.operation: Classify a residue by existence of a square root modulo p.
examples: 4 is a quadratic residue mod 7 because 2^2 congruent 4 mod 7
counterexamples: Declaring every nonzero residue class a square mod p is invalid

rules.name: p-adic valuation additivity on products
preconditions: a and b are nonzero integers
p is prime
rules.operation: Add p-adic valuations across products.
counterexamples: Treating valuations as additive over sums in general is invalid
